newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt enjoys strong poll lead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt enjoys strong poll lead.

text.p: The Australian government has entered its second year in office with a substantial 13 point lead over the Labor opposition, according to a newspaper poll published on Tuesday.

The government's primary support rose four percentage points from The Australian's last poll two weeks ago to 49 percent, while Labor's support fell two points to 36 percent, The Australian's Newspoll found.
As preferred prime minister, John Howard's lead over opposition leader Kim Beazley increased four points to 53 percent, while Beazley's rating fell one point to 23 percent.
But 24 percent of those surveyed remained uncommitted.
The latest result compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election that saw Howard sweep into power, ending 13 years of Labor rule.
The Newspoll surveyed 1,145 voters around the country by telephone last weekend.
